children: has shipped more than 100mn PlayStation 5 consoles worldwide, roughly six years after the machine went on sale in November 2020,
reported on November 14. The cumulative total passed the milestone earlier this week.

The figure comes as the Japanese electronics and entertainment group has shifted its gaming focus. In recent years Sony has given priority to its subscription service, which lets customers download games online, over pushing hardware sales.

The PS5 gained a following among players for its sharp graphics and 3D audio, which the company promoted as delivering an immersive experience. The console cost JPY54,978 (about $520 at the time) when it was launched in Japan.

Early sales were faster than for any of the five PlayStation generations. The PS5 reached 10mn units in July 2021, about eight months after release. Two factors drove that pace. The console arrived seven years after the PS4, its predecessor, and the COVID-19 pandemic kept people at home and pushed up demand for home entertainment.
Supply could not keep up. A shortage of the semiconductors used in the console, combined with disruption to logistics networks, left the PS5 scarce for about two years after its debut.

title: Japan's Sony ships 100mn PlayStation 5 consoles worldwide
